sections.title: Purpose and setup
sections.what: Explains that the script rebuilds the 3D element library and sets the paths to the Blender script, the output folder, and the project root.
sections.why: Makes clear that the output is committed and that this script is only run when the source changes.
sections.watch_out: The paths are computed from this file's location, so moving the file breaks them.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Run Blender or fall back to nix-shell
sections.what: Checks whether a blender program is available. If it is, runs the Blender script with the output folder as an argument. Otherwise it asks nix-shell to start Blender and run the same script.
sections.why: Likely reason: developers may or may not have Blender installed, so the script handles both cases.
sections.watch_out: The fallback joins arguments into one shell string, so unusual characters in the path can break the command.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Command entry point
sections.what: Runs the main function and passes its result to the system as the exit code when the file is run directly.
sections.why: Lets the shell see whether the rebuild succeeded.
sections.watch_out: Importing this file does not run the build, so only direct runs regenerate the models.

summary: A helper that rebuilds the committed 3D element library by running a Blender script in headless mode, using a local Blender if present or a Nix package otherwise.
purpose: Lets the developer regenerate the detailed 3D shape files that the web app ships with, without installing Blender by hand.
why: Likely reason: the library files are committed, so the app never needs Blender at run time, and this script is only run when the source script changes.
how: It looks for a Blender program on the system path. If found, it runs the Blender script in background mode with startup settings off. If not, it runs the same command through nix-shell with Blender installed, then returns Blender's exit code.
inputs: The Blender script in assets/blender and the output folder frontend/public/models.
outputs: Updated GLB model files in frontend/public/models, and the exit code of the Blender run.
risks: The fallback builds a command with single quotes, so a path containing an apostrophe would break it. It needs Blender or nix-shell to be installed.
debug: If the run fails, look at the printed Blender output for Python errors, and confirm that nix-shell and the script path exist. Check the exit code returned to the shell.
